precepts.text: Every wise woman buildeth her house: but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands. Instead of watching what that other husband is doing, study that wise woman. Go ask her: what are you doing? Why is he so happy? Every time you ask for something, he gives it; what is the secret? She has a mind to what is going on in her house: these are the things I need to fix to make my household better, this is how I assist my husband. That is the desire of Genesis: she shall desire her husband. That means studying him: you know what he likes, his dislikes, when to leave him be, and when to come speak. But pride, sister, will keep you from doing it. You think he is supposed to give you everything first before you do what you do as a wife; that is not what you are in the marriage for. You do your job, and that man does his job. And if reciprocation only flows one way, you might be the reason your marriage is the way it is.
precepts.point: Which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith. And a lot of you women in marriages covet other people's marriages based on what they have. You see somebody else with a big house and feel your marriage is inadequate; they got a new car, they go on trips, why are we not doing that? But what are you doing to fix the things in your own marriage? You do not know what they have been through: they may have struggled fifteen or twenty years before any financial establishment came into that relationship. You see the here and now, not the hardships and the pain on the way. You think the grass is greener, and you do not know what happens in that house at night. When you desire what another man is doing in his house, you are coveting, breaking the ten commandments.
precepts.why:
“which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith”. A lot of sisters in marriages covet other people's marriages: he's doing this, he's doing that, and you're mad at your husband because he isn't doing what that brother is doing, when he is probably trying to get where he needs to be. Solomon points you somewhere else: “Every wise woman buildeth her house”.

You're looking at the wrong thing. Instead of watching what that husband is doing, study her. Why don't you go ask her: what are you doing? What's the secret? Why is he so happy? Every time you ask for something he gives it; I see you with the new purse, the new shoes. Ask her how she's building her house up.

The wise woman has a mind to what is going on in the house: these are the things I need to fix to make my household better; this is how I assist my husband. That is why Genesis says her desire shall be to her husband. It means you study him: you know his likes and dislikes, what irritates him, when not to mess with him, and when to come say something. You live in the house; you see it all the time.

“but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands.” Your pride, sister, will keep you from doing it. You think he's supposed to give you everything first before you get on board: if he ain't doing this for me, I ain't doing nothing for him. You're out of your damn mind; that isn't what you're in the marriage for. He is out providing, bringing food into the house, clothes for the kids, paying the bills. You do your job and he does his. If he has to do it all before you reciprocate anything, something's wrong, and you might be the reason your marriage is the way it is.

precepts.text: The heart knoweth his own bitterness: you cannot play confused when somebody asks where the bitterness is coming from. Nobody else can get in and decipher exactly what it is; we can tell you, brother, you are off, there is sin in there, but you know the specifics of what you are dealing with.
precepts.point: Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves: not your neighbor. Yourself.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
“Examine yourselves”: not your neighbor, yourself. And you can do it, because “The heart knoweth his own bitterness”. Your mind knows its own bitterness. Brother, sister, you can't play confused when somebody asks, man, where is that bitterness coming from?

“and a stranger doth not intermeddle with his joy.” So you can't say, oh Bishop, tell me what's going on with me. You know exactly what is going on in your mind. Nobody else can get in and decipher exactly what it is. We can say, brother, you're off, you ain't moving right, there is sin in there; we may not know it specifically, but you know the specifics of what you are dealing with.

This is a heavy topic. A lot of brothers and sisters are bitter. It came up in our congregation with a brother dealing with his wife, and then we came down here and saw the same thing, and it destroyed a household. If that spirit is left unchecked it can destroy the congregation. That is why each of us has to prove our own self: the heart already knows where the bitterness is.

precepts.text: Cursed be the man that trusteth in man and maketh flesh his arm: a sister who says I trust him instead of seeing the test results is cursed in her trust.
precepts.point: An STD test is the example: six months of excuses about insurance and work is a red flag, and you wake up with the love bump because you were so worried about laying down with her. Refusing a test is hiding something; get multiple tests and go to the hospital with them, because people fake results with AI.

note.label: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

precepts.why:
“The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way: but the folly of fools is deceit.” The fool deceives himself and ignores the red flags. One of the plainest is trust in place of proof. Bishop Yawsaw told of a situation, and it is happening all over the nation: a sister was asked, Did y’all show each other your STD test results? She said, I trust him.

“Thus saith the Lord; Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm.” Miss me with the trust. I trust God. When you make flesh your arm, you make another human being your strength, the one you rely on and believe in. No: I need to see the test.

It is a red flag if someone does not want to go get tested. What do you have to hide? What are you scared of? If you have not been doing anything, you have nothing to hide; but if you are nasty, now you are scared and running from the truth. Six or seven months of excuses, I had to work, something happened with my insurance, and then you wake up with the love bump, because you were so worried about laying down with the sister that you did not care that she never took the test.

In this present world there need to be multiple tests, and you have to go to the hospital with them, because people are sending someone else in or having AI make them an STD chart, and you think it is official. That is the prudent man understanding his way. The sister who says I trust him has made flesh her arm, and the scripture says that trust is cursed.

precepts.text: This witness is true; wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith. Our job is to rebuke our people sharply so they repent.
precepts.point: I do not trust you, because you do not know the scriptures and you have not put in the work, and God who called you does not trust you either. When persecution shows up you will be the first to turn against us, for one piece of silver rather than thirty.
precepts.why:
“A true witness delivereth souls”: a true prophet, a true servant, delivers souls. Paul shows how a true witness does it: “This witness is true. Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith.”

It is our job, brothers, to rebuke our people sharply. Why? That they may be sound in the faith; that they may repent. That is how souls are delivered.

So whose soul have you been delivering? You have been sitting here five years, seven years, ten years; some of you cannot even deliver your own soul, because you forgot the mission. Who are you working for, spiritually: Messiah or Satan? Some of you are agents working for Esau.

“but a deceitful witness speaketh lies.” Our people love lies, and the deceitful witness feeds them lies. That is why you see ten thousand, twenty thousand in the Christian churches: they do not want the truth. They say Christ cannot be black, Christ cannot come only for the Israelite. The truth to us is a foreign language. That is why the true witness has to rebuke sharply: sharp rebuke is what brings a people who love lies to repentance.

precepts.text: Whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son. Conform means change. We can see the potential in a brother, but you have to see it yourself; a deacon's job is to push your spirit, not to see it for you.
precepts.point: I do not trust you, because you do not know the scriptures and you have not put in the work, and God who called you does not trust you either. When persecution shows up you will be the first to turn against us, for one piece of silver rather than thirty.
precepts.why:
“In the fear of the Lord is strong confidence.” Some of you have no confidence and low self-esteem because you have no fear of God, sitting in the same seat for seven years. Romans shows what God called you for: “For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.”

What does it mean to be conformed? To change. We must change to the image of Jesus Christ. Some of you have not changed yet, and we can see it.

We can see the potential on you: this brother has the spirit to do great things in Israel. But you have to see it. My job as a deacon is to push your spirit and to build you up, but no matter how much I build you up, if you cannot see it, I cannot make you see it. You have to get up and see it yourself.

There is a lot of work to do while you are waiting for the kingdom, and the kingdom does not come by observation. When temptation and tribulation come, the one who has not been conformed will run, because mentally and spiritually he is not strong enough to endure it. Being predestinated to be conformed means you have to do the changing.

precepts.text: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself.
precepts.point: I do not trust you, because you do not know the scriptures and you have not put in the work, and God who called you does not trust you either. When persecution shows up you will be the first to turn against us, for one piece of silver rather than thirty.
precepts.why:
“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will.” The same God who foreknew us and predestinated us to be conformed to the image of his Son predestinated us unto the adoption of children, by Jesus Christ, to himself.

That calling is what the class carried straight into Paul: “For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of: for necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!” Paul understood he was a servant, sent to serve the people and deliver souls. Destruction unto me if I do not do what I was sent to do.

“For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward.” You have to do it willingly, not because somebody forced you; a brother forced to do something has no spirit in it. Yet some of you get up at four in the morning and willingly give the white man eight or twelve hours without complaining, while coming here on the Sabbath is a burden.

So being predestinated as children by Jesus Christ is not a reason to sit and wait. God did not call you here just to sit and listen. It is a call to be the true witness that delivers souls, and in the fear of the Lord is the strong confidence to do it.

precepts.text: The king's favour is toward a wise servant; that is what David was as armourbearer. We know him as a mighty king, but he started out a wise servant, and that is how he got the king's favour.
precepts.point: Saul asked Jesse to let David stand before him, for he hath found favour in my sight; Saul liked the spirit on that young brother, and every king keeps a young soldier always with him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
Saul sent to Jesse, “Send me David thy son, which is with the sheep.” Jesse sent David with “an ass laden with bread, and a bottle of wine, and a kid”, and “David came to Saul, and stood before him: and he loved him greatly; and he became his armourbearer.”

These are David’s humble beginnings, serving at the king’s side. Even after the spirit had left Saul, David loved him and served him faithfully. Saul sent again, “Let David, I pray thee, stand before me; for he hath found favour in my sight.” Saul liked the spirit on that young brother, and every king keeps a young soldier always with him.

“The king’s favour is toward a wise servant: but his wrath is against him that causeth shame.” That is what David was as armourbearer. We know him as a mighty king, but he started out a wise servant, and that is how he got the king’s favour.

precepts.text: In all labor there is profit, but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury.
precepts.point: For thou shalt eat the labor of thine hands. There is profit in laboring, and this is not just the nine to five, it is laboring in this truth. We have too many people in IUIC who just talk and do not labor at all, and shame on you. You will escape this world by your works.

note.label: Psalm 128: Blessed Is Every One That Feareth the Lord

precepts.why:
“In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury.” The one that feareth the Lord shall eat the labor of his hands. There is profit in laboring, and this is not just the nine to five, it is laboring in this truth.

We have too many people in IUIC who just talk and do not labor at all, and shame on you. The talk of the lips tendeth only to penury. You will escape this world by your works.

precepts.text: The fear of the Most High is the beginning of wisdom.
precepts.point: A faithful witness will not lie, but a false witness utters lies. A scorner seeks wisdom and cannot find it, but knowledge is easy to the one who understands. To get the understanding you fear the Most High and keep the commandments.
precepts.why:
“A scorner seeketh wisdom, and findeth it not: but knowledge is easy unto him that understandeth.” How do you get the understanding? “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.”

You fear the Most High and keep the commandments. The scorner seeks wisdom without the fear of the Lord and cannot find it; the one who does his commandments has a good understanding, and knowledge is easy to him.

precepts.text: Observe the time when you are among the indiscreet.
precepts.point: The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way, but the folly of fools is deceit. Fools make a mock at sin, but among the righteous there is favor.
precepts.why:
“Go from the presence of a foolish man, when thou perceivest not in him the lips of knowledge.” This is why the scripture says: “If thou be among the indiscreet, observe the time; but be continually among men of understanding.”

When you are among the indiscreet, observe the time; when you perceive there are no lips of knowledge in a man, go from his presence and be continually among men of understanding.

precepts.text: When a rich man speaks all listen, but the poor man is dismissed.
precepts.point: The poor is hated even by his own neighbor, but the rich have many friends. Ecclesiasticus says the same: when the rich man speaks everybody holds their tongue, but when the poor man speaks they ask who is this.
precepts.why:
“The poor is hated even of his own neighbour: but the rich hath many friends.” Ecclesiasticus says the same: “When a rich man speaketh, every man holdeth his tongue, and, look, what he saith, they extol it to the clouds: but if the poor man speak, they say, What fellow is this? and if he stumble, they will help to overthrow him.”

When the rich man speaks everybody holds their tongue and extols what he says, but when the poor man speaks they ask who is this, and if he stumbles they help to overthrow him. The rich has many friends; the poor is dismissed even by his own neighbour.

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

precepts.why:
“The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib”. Those are dumb animals, but even the dumbest animals know their owners. “but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.” Our people don't know their owner or consider that they're the Israelites, that their forefathers are Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

“Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity”. That's us, laden with sin. “a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters”. A lot of us think we're righteous; God calls us a seed of evildoers. “they have forsaken the Lord”. We've forsaken God's laws and turned our backs on the Most High. You can see it today. Christians talk as if they aren't in sin, but they're worshiping idols. You're not in the truth. Repent and come out of those evil churches or the Most High will bring judgment and you will die. I'm not sugarcoating nothing.

“they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger”. Deuteronomy 28 shows that anger. The Most High took us down as a great nation. Esau and social media make slavery seem like a small thing. Those who control the narrative control the mind. What they put in front of you shapes what you think. Donald Trump is erasing black history little by little, taking things down, saying it was the past and today's white people didn't do it. He's doing it so cunningly some of you don't catch it. That's the devil for you. No Christian pastor talks about what he's doing. They're all in it together, all getting paid. He's erasing it right in front of our eyes. “they are gone away backward.” We turned away, and the Most High took us down.

Knowledge is easy to him that understands, that keeps the commandments.

Every wise woman buildeth her house. So it says every wise woman builds her house. So guess what? Every wise woman builds her house. You sisters have to learn, as wives, as Israelite women, to build your house. That's why you get around senior women. You get around them. You speak to them. Learn how to build your house. Get me Sirach 26 and verse 13.

note.label: Final Call: Message to the Black Man

points: Every wise woman buildeth her house: but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands. So a wise woman — the actions they do when they withhold affection, that is when they start breaking down the house. That is like the man who is angry and starts breaking things in his own house physically. That is stupid. There is no way I pay money for my TV and my walls and my furniture and I am going to start breaking it because I am mad at you. Then I have got to fix it. Or you are so broke you cannot fix it, so you have got holes in the wall.
Spiritually, the woman then starts to break down her house, because she is going to create more division and widen the gap and make her husband go cold for her.

So if you want to show that you have the wisdom that you do, you build your house. And you build your house by applying 1 Peter 3. You build your house by applying all the other verses like in Ephesians 5 and Proverbs 31. You go back to Genesis and you look at those things, because what happens is we tend to lose meaning in the everyday. Though you may know once someone tells you — it is like when you get a question and you know the answer, you just cannot recall it, and then when the answer is given you think, oh, I should have known that. That should not happen in the household.

That is what it means to meditate on verses. You meditate on the verses for the thing that you are dealing with. And meditate does not mean just read it once, or yeah, I know what it says. It means truly reflect on it and let it resonate with your spirit, so that that inner man built up after Christ is what shows forth, and not the carnal, worldly, conditioned, pre-programmed brother or sister.

So what you have got to ask yourself is, what am I building? Not, what did it take for me to respond this way to the man that is supposed to be my head, whom I am supposed to reverence and submit to as unto the Lord. What am I building right now? Because once you understand it, now you need to make the choice: am I going to build, or am I going to tear down? And as a wife and helpmeet, to be a pillar of rest means you do not let that thing get torn down, and you certainly do not do it yourself.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife

points: He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding: but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly. He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding. Great understanding in what? The Bible, the scriptures, the law.

But he that is hasty of spirit. Some of you have what you call anger issues, and you brought that thing into the truth with you. You have been sitting here two years, three years, four years, five years, and you have not got rid of it yet. And some of you are using it as an excuse. We have seen it with men. We have seen it with women.

You know the old Mike Tyson, when he gets in the ring his hands are like this. You know why boxers put their hands like that? To defend himself. That is you. You walk into your house like a boxer. You are waiting. As soon as your wife says something, it does not matter if it is something good or bad, you jump. She says shalom and you say, why are you saying shalom to me for? You cannot control it because of your trauma. You bring your job into your house. You have been angry at your job all day. What you need to do is leave that spirit outside that door before you walk into the house.

And sisters too. You think your husband is trying to attack you. He is about to leave for work, he is about to give you a kiss, and you say, whoa, what is going on here, my first husband never kissed me before he went to work, why are you kissing me? Trauma. You want to go to a movie? What do you mean? My husband never took me anywhere. You want to go on vacation? I never went anywhere. Sis, you do not have to cook today, I am going to take you out. Whoa, you must want something, what do you want? Trauma. The brother tries to do something good for you, but because of your past relationship you cannot receive it. Those are the things we see in the truth, because you never let go of the past.

And if you are like that in the house with your wife or your husband, you come here and you are going to be the same way with brothers and sisters. You go in the street and you are going to be the same with the people. Quick to snap. And you are going to be the same with your kids. He cannot go play outside. Why? I do not want him to play outside. She is in punishment, she can have pancakes, no syrup. He is in punishment, he can have salad, no salad dressing. Something is wrong with you. Those things happen in the midst of us, and we are not going to sweep it under the rug like it is not happening.

And you stand there while we are telling you that is not normal, and you look at us like we are the ones who are crazy. Sometimes I have to ask the brother next to me, am I crazy? Is something wrong with me? Because this dude is trying to convince me it is me and not him. And then Bishop says, hey, you are an officer of ten, you think you can lead ten men? And you look at Bishop dead in the eye and say yes. And we all look at each other like, what is wrong with this guy? No, you cannot lead men. If you are treating your wife and your children like that, you think you can lead men?

A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones. A sound heart is talking about the mind. A sound mind, the right mind, is the life of the flesh, the life of the body. When you are in the right frame of mind you can do a lot, because sometimes you cannot even fall asleep because you are not in the right frame of mind. You let little things bother you. Stress is what is going to kill you. It is not this truth. Stress is going to kill you because you are always stressed about everything.

In other words you never have a peaceful mind, because the whole body starts with a peaceful mind. You are always angry. Some of you do not know how to spell peace. You did not come here for drama, you came here for peace. God is a God of peace. He brings peace. When you pray, ask God for peace in your household, peace with your wife, peace with your husband. Because the peace starts here. If you do not have peace here, the rest of your body has no peace.

But envy the rottenness of the bones. Yes, the white man is the devil. But not one of us here can be kept from getting the kingdom by the white man. Not one. So who is the biggest enemy? You are. You are your own biggest enemy, because only you can keep yourself from getting the kingdom. So who are you fighting against? You are fighting against yourself. Only you can remove your name out of the book of life. The white man does not have that power. But you have that power. So it is called self-destruct.
Every wise woman buildeth her house: but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands. You pluck it down by complaining, yelling, arguing, and being disrespectful.
The simple believeth every word: we can't be simple, family. We cannot be simple. But the prudent man looketh well to his going: that's how we got to be.

There is a way which seemeth right unto a man. In our mind we think it is the right thing: this sounds real good. But the end thereof are the ways of death: at the end is death and destruction, because you have no discernment of what is going on.
Every time you counsel with yourself, you are going to be 100 percent right every time. You are always going to be right in your own mind.

Every wise woman buildeth her house: but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands. Wisdom is according to the commandments. A foolish woman is going to use her own hands to find her own man and do her own thing; she ain't going to listen to what the scriptures say.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death: the one who takes notes for hours and then does the exact opposite, because he is grown and nobody has walked in his shoes, often at half your age.

That death may not be instant; it can be a lifetime of heartache and even bloodshed. Counsel comes from those who have been through it, and if I have not seen your situation I send you to somebody who has.

Many relationships feel right but are spiritually wrong. Proving is finding out whether God sent this person, more than a credit check for a car, and the signs are put in front of you months before you pretend to be surprised.
Sisters, this man will be your head and your lord with more power than your daddy had, so vet him; and do not confuse the stages of attraction for love because you met her last week.

The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.

The poor is hated even by his own neighbor, but the rich have many friends. Ecclesiasticus says the same: when the rich man speaks everybody holds their tongue, but when the poor man speaks they ask who is this.
He that despises his neighbor sins, but he that has mercy on the poor is happy.
Those who devise evil go astray, but mercy and truth belong to those who devise good. In all labor there is profit, but mere talk of the lips tends only to poverty.
The crown of the wise is their riches, but the foolishness of fools is folly. A true witness delivers souls, but a deceitful witness speaks lies.
In the fear of the Most High is strong confidence, and his children shall have a place of refuge.
The fear of the Most High is a fountain of life to depart from the snares of death.
In the multitude of people is the king's honor, but in the lack of people is the destruction of the prince. He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding, but the hasty of spirit exalts folly.
A sound heart is the life of the flesh, but envy is the rottenness of the bones.
He that oppresses the poor reproaches his Maker, but he that honors him has mercy on the poor. The wicked is driven away in his wickedness, but the righteous has hope in his death.
Wisdom rests in the heart of the one who has understanding, but what is in the midst of fools is made known.

Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a reproach to any people. God's laws will exalt us as a nation. Why do we go through slavery and sit at the bottom of the barrel? Sin. Sin is a reproach to any people.
The king's favor is toward the wise servant, but his wrath is against the one who causes shame.

“Righteousness exalteth a nation”. We weren't always in this condition. There was a time we were the most righteous people on earth, and there was also a time we were the most wicked. Now a lot of us are waking up to who we are. “but sin is a reproach to any people.” The Most High took us down because of sin, not because we were righteous and somebody attacked us for no reason. He sent the Assyrians against the northern kingdom because they were evil as hell. He sent the Babylonians against us because we were evil as hell. If we were righteous, we would never have been taken down. No nation can survive in sin. We're talking about Israel, the twelve tribes.

Moses delivered us from Egypt; we were in the wilderness forty years. Then came David and Solomon. After Solomon, the kingdom split, and the whole twelve tribes have never been together again. Christ's purpose is to bring the southern and northern kingdoms back together. Deuteronomy 28 was a prophecy given in the wilderness before David and Solomon, not something that all happened in their time. The Bible isn't written in order. Those curses happened later. We didn't believe it, but it happened.
